result.title: The Accuracy Well: Nonmonotone Accuracy Dynamics at Vanishing Initialization
result.summary: We study classification dynamics under small initialization and identify a pronounced non-monotone behavior of accuracy that we call the accuracy well: accuracy rises rapidly early in training, subsequently drops, and only much later recovers. We observe this phenomenon in deep linear networks, fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST, deep convolutional networks on CIFAR-10, and controlled synthetic tasks, across different losses and optimizers and in both training and test accuracy. We propose a three-stage explanation in terms of target-driven organization, a degeneracy bottleneck, and subsequent recruitment and recovery. We develop a rigorous theory of these dynamics for shallow and deep linear networks, showing in particular that high accuracy can emerge while the predictor and the change in loss remain asymptotically vanishing, before continued optimization causes accuracy to deteriorate. For a simple synthetic classification task, we prove an extreme instance in which accuracy asymptotically rises to 100%, collapses to 0, and later recovers permanently to 100%. Our results show that classification accuracy can reveal aspects of learning dynamics that are not captured by the training loss alone.

AI.brief_summary: 在小初始化条件下研究分类精度的非单调动态，提出「精度井」现象（先快速上升、随后下降、很久后恢复），在深层线性网络、MNIST/CIFAR 网络与合成任务上观察，并给出「目标驱动组织—退化瓶颈—重新招募恢复」的三阶段解释及线性网络理论。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文指出精度可揭示损失无法反映的训练动态，这一「指标非单调、损失近乎不变」的解耦视角可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的评价与监督提供类比线索：仅凭 loss 或状态收敛判断推理质量或许会遗漏行为变化，可供核查。
